title: 1950 AHSME Problem 46
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AB=12,\) \(AC=7,\) and \(BC=10.\) If sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) are doubled while \(BC\) remains the same, then:

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: The area is four times the original area

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: The area of the triangle is \(0\)

solutions.text:
The new side lengths are \(24,\) \(14,\) and \(10.\) Because \[ 14+10=24, \] they form a degenerate triangle: all three vertices are collinear. Its area is therefore \(0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write down the three new side lengths
Compare the largest new side with the sum of the other two
